title: Action Budgets, Iteration Caps, and Cost Governors

questions.question: Which token cost does turn_cost use at turn 30?
options: 2,500 tokens, because loop pricing starts at turn 31
10,000 tokens, the request cap
8,000 tokens, because LOOP_STARTS_AT is 30
500 tokens, the monthly average
questions.explanation: The implementation checks turn >= LOOP_STARTS_AT, so turn 30 is charged LOOP_TURN_TOKENS = 8,000.

questions.question: When does velocity_exceeded return true for a rolling window?
options: At exactly the configured rate
Whenever monthly spend is nonzero
Whenever the current turn is at least 30
Only when dollars per minute is strictly greater than velocity_usd_per_min
questions.explanation: The guard compares the computed rolling rate with >, not >=; reaching the limit exactly does not trigger this check.

questions.question: What does the default session budget of $50 constrain?
options: Total spend for one simulated run, stopping once dollars reach the cap
Spend across all months and all users
Only the token count of one request
The number of files an action can edit
questions.explanation: simulate checks dollars >= max_budget_usd for the current Run, separate from per-request, iteration, velocity, and monthly controls.

questions.question: Why does the no-caps 10,000-turn run report about $239.52 rather than $500?
options: The monthly cap silently halves every request
Its token pricing totals below the $500 monthly_cap_usd, so that cap is not reached
The first 30 turns are free
The simulator counts only failed turns
questions.explanation: The run charges 2,500 tokens before turn 30 and 8,000 afterward at $0.003 per thousand; the resulting total is about $239.52, below $500.

questions.question: What does a layered Governor do when several caps are enabled?
options: It ignores the first cap and always runs 10,000 turns
It increases max_tokens_per_request after turn 30
It stops at the first enabled limit reached and records stopped_by
It applies only the monthly cap
questions.explanation: simulate checks enabled iteration, session, velocity, and monthly limits after each turn and records the first one that trips.

questions.question: Which distinction is central to the governor design?
options: All limits operate on the same time scale
Only dollars matter; tokens are informational
Velocity is checked once after the whole run
A request token cap, iteration cap, velocity window, session budget, and monthly cap constrain different failure modes
questions.explanation: The governor layers independent controls: request size, turn count, short-term spend rate, run spend, and monthly spend address different runaway patterns.
